english: I have not had breakfast yet this morning.
tip: belum means 'not yet' and implies it will still happen: Saya belum sarapan = I haven't had breakfast yet. Even 'are you married?' is answered with belum, not tidak.

english: Dad has not come home from the office yet.
tip: Belum, not tidak: belum pulang = not home yet, still expected. Tidak pulang would mean he isn't coming home at all.

english: Mom is cooking in the kitchen.
tip: sedang marks action in progress: Ibu sedang memasak. (Mom is cooking right now.)

target: Saya akan pergi ke pasar besok pagi.
english: I will go to the market tomorrow morning.
tip: akan puts a sentence in the future without touching the verb: Saya akan pergi = I will go. pergi keeps the same form in past, present, and future.

target: Dia akan mulai pekerjaan baru bulan depan.
english: She will start a new job next month.
tip: Akan is optional once a time word sets the future – with bulan depan in the sentence, Dia mulai pekerjaan baru bulan depan works fine too.

english: The plane will arrive shortly.
tip: Sebentar lagi is literally 'a moment more' – lagi after a time span means that far from now: seminggu lagi = in a week.

english: I just woke up.
tip: Baru literally means new – baru saja bangun is 'newly woke up', so baru (saja) before a verb = just did it.

english: Dad is still working at the office.
tip: masih = still, the action continues: Dia masih bekerja. (He is still working.)

target: Saya pernah pergi ke Bali dua kali.
english: I have been to Bali twice.
tip: pernah = have ever done at least once: Saya pernah ke Bali. (I have been to Bali.)

english: He has never been on a plane.
tip: belum pernah = never so far: Dia belum pernah naik pesawat. (He has never flown.)

english: Where do you live now?
tip: Question words can stay in place: Kamu tinggal di mana? is literally 'You live where?' – unlike English, di mana doesn't have to move to the front.

target: Ke mana kamu pergi hari ini?
english: Where are you going today?
tip: ke mana asks where to (motion): Ke mana kamu pergi? (Where are you going?)

english: Where does this bus go?
tip: Destination questions can drop the verb: Bus ini ke mana? (Where does this bus go?)

target: Harga tiket masuk lima puluh ribu rupiah.
english: The entrance ticket costs fifty thousand rupiah.
tip: Tens stack simply: lima puluh = five tens = 50, dua puluh = 20.

target: Kopi ini harganya dua puluh lima ribu.
english: This coffee costs twenty-five thousand.
tip: harganya = harga + -nya ('its price'): Kopi ini harganya... is literally 'This coffee, its price 25 thousand' – no verb needed.

target: Ada empat orang di keluarga saya.
english: There are four people in my family.
tip: ada = there is/are: Ada empat orang. (There are four people.)

target: Saya mau beli tiga kilo beras.
english: I want to buy three kilos of rice.
tip: After mau, the bare root is natural in speech: mau beli = want to buy.

target: Kamar ini seratus ribu rupiah semalam.
english: This room is one hundred thousand rupiah a night.
tip: se- means one: seratus = one hundred, semalam = one night.

english: What time is it there now?
tip: Order matters: jam berapa = what time, berapa jam = how many hours. Jam berapa sekarang? asks for the clock time, not a duration.

english: It is nine in the morning now.
tip: Time of day follows the hour: jam sembilan pagi = 9 a.m., jam sembilan malam = 9 p.m.

target: Kereta ke Bandung datang jam tiga sore.
english: The train to Bandung arrives at three in the afternoon.
tip: sore = late afternoon, about 3-6 p.m.: jam tiga sore = 3 p.m.

english: Today is Monday, isn't it?
tip: Days take hari first: hari Senin = Monday, hari Sabtu = Saturday.

target: Dia mencuci muka di kamar mandi.
english: She washes her face in the bathroom.
tip: Before c, meN- becomes men-: cuci → mencuci (wash).

target: Ibu memasak nasi goreng untuk sarapan.
english: Mom cooks fried rice for breakfast.
tip: Roots starting with m keep a simple me-: masak → memasak (cook).

target: Saya menulis catatan di buku kecil.
english: I write notes in a small book.
tip: Before t, meN- becomes men- and the t drops: tulis → menulis (write).

english: Dad reads the newspaper every morning.
tip: Before b, meN- becomes mem- and the b stays: baca → membaca (read).

english: She sweeps the floor before leaving.
tip: Before s, meN- becomes meny- and the s drops: sapu → menyapu (sweep).

english: I take a towel from the cupboard.
tip: Vowel-first roots take meng-: ambil → mengambil (take).

english: I am reading a new book.
tip: Indonesian verbs never change for -ing – sedang does the job: sedang membaca = in the middle of reading. Drop sedang and it just means 'read'.

target: Dia sudah bangun sebelum matahari terbit.
english: He already woke up before sunrise.
tip: No past tense here – sudah bangun is literally 'already wake'. sudah marks the action as finished; the verb bangun itself never changes.
